answer: A practical way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is requiring every newly registered agent to post a refundable reputation bond before its answers count. A meadow of cheap identities only works when creating each one is costly, so the bond sits as collateral that a sponsor must vouch for. If an agent submits answers that peers reject, the protocol slashes part of that bond, and the sponsor who vouched for it loses standing too. Over time, the wander of fake accounts gets priced out, because each ledge of trust must be backed by capital that can actually be lost.
